business_problem: PLAID needed to support large volumes of real-time customer-behavior data without forcing its engineering and SRE teams to spend increasing amounts of time operating self-hosted multi-cloud databases.
solution_summary: PLAID migrated the databases behind its KARTE platform to MongoDB Atlas on Google Cloud so real-time behavioral analytics and multi-cloud operations could scale cleanly. KARTE products such as Insight and Datahub accumulate user activity from many digital touchpoints and turn it into recommendations and customer views in less than a second, which means the underlying database has to sustain very high read and write rates while staying flexible. Atlas now lets development teams provision clusters through Terraform integrations instead of routing requests through a small SRE group, and it automates upgrades, backups, alerts, and performance diagnostics that previously consumed operational bandwidth. PLAID also combines Atlas with Google Cloud services such as GKE, BigQuery, Bigtable, GCE, and Anthos, giving the company a multi-cloud data architecture that is easier to operate while still supporting tens of thousands of reads and writes per second for real-time customer analytics.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Runs the core document databases behind PLAID's KARTE behavioral-analytics products.

solution_components.name: Google Cloud
solution_components.role: Hosts the Atlas deployment and related cloud services used by PLAID's multi-cloud analytics environment.

data_flow: Customer interaction data enters PLAID's KARTE products, MongoDB Atlas stores and serves the behavioral records that drive real-time analytics and recommendations, and downstream Google Cloud services consume or enrich that data for broader customer-view and datahub capabilities.
business_outcome: PLAID reduced operational toil, improved stability, and accelerated development so teams can focus more on customer-facing product value and less on keeping databases running.
